refs.note: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter in — but he that doeth the will of my Father

refs.note: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus

refs.label: Revelation 22:14
refs.note: Blessed are they that do his commandments

refs.label: 1 Enoch 1:9
refs.note: Quote: Jude 1:14-15. Jude says Enoch prophesied these words, then quotes them. This is the clearest quote of a book outside the 66-book Bible.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 10:4-6
refs.note: Parallel: Jude 1:6. Jude 6 speaks of angels who left their place and are kept in chains of darkness until the great day of judgment. 1 Enoch tells of the Watchers who sinned and were bound until the judgment.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 10:11-13
refs.note: Parallel: Jude 1:6. Jude 6 speaks of angels who left their place and are kept in chains of darkness until the great day of judgment. 1 Enoch tells of the Watchers who sinned and were bound until the judgment.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 12:4
refs.note: Parallel: Jude 1:6. Jude 6 speaks of angels who left their place and are kept in chains of darkness until the great day of judgment. 1 Enoch tells of the Watchers who sinned and were bound until the judgment.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 10:12-14
refs.note: Parallel: 1 Peter 3:19-20. Christ preaching to the “spirits in prison” is often compared with Enoch's message to the imprisoned Watchers. Scholars disagree about how closely the two are linked.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 12:4-6
refs.note: Parallel: 1 Peter 3:19-20. Christ preaching to the “spirits in prison” is often compared with Enoch's message to the imprisoned Watchers. Scholars disagree about how closely the two are linked.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 21:10
refs.note: Parallel: 1 Peter 3:19-20. Christ preaching to the “spirits in prison” is often compared with Enoch's message to the imprisoned Watchers. Scholars disagree about how closely the two are linked.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 18:13-16
refs.note: Allusion: Jude 1:13. “Wandering stars” kept in blackness of darkness echo the stars that broke God's command in 1 Enoch.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 21:3-6
refs.note: Allusion: Jude 1:13. “Wandering stars” kept in blackness of darkness echo the stars that broke God's command in 1 Enoch.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 5:4
refs.note: Allusion: Jude 1:16. Jude's grumblers whose mouths speak proud things echo this verse in 1 Enoch.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 6:1-2
refs.note: Expands: Genesis 6:1-4. Genesis 6:1-4 briefly mentions the sons of God and the daughters of men. 1 Enoch tells that story at length. It is not a quote.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 7:1-2
refs.note: Expands: Genesis 6:1-4. Genesis 6:1-4 briefly mentions the sons of God and the daughters of men. 1 Enoch tells that story at length. It is not a quote.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 12:1-4
refs.note: Expands: Genesis 5:21-24. Genesis says Enoch walked with God and was taken. 1 Enoch tells what Enoch saw and said. It is not a quote.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 62:2-3
refs.note: Allusion: Matthew 25:31. The Son of Man sitting on his glorious throne to judge is close to the Son of Man on his throne in 1 Enoch's Parables.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 69:27-29
refs.note: Allusion: Matthew 25:31. The Son of Man sitting on his glorious throne to judge is close to the Son of Man on his throne in 1 Enoch's Parables.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 69:27
refs.note: Parallel: John 5:22 + John 5:27. The Father giving judgment to the Son of Man is similar to the Son of Man judging in 1 Enoch.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 38:2
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 26:24. Jesus saying it would be better for that man not to have been born is close to the last line of this verse in 1 Enoch.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 5:5
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 5:5. “Inherit the earth” appears in both (it is in the part of this verse marked 6a-7 in our text). The main source for Jesus' words is Psalm 37:11, so this is only a similar phrase.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 94:8
refs.note: Parallel: Luke 6:24. “Woe to you who are rich” is close to the woes on the rich in 1 Enoch 94.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 39:4
refs.note: Allusion: Luke 16:9. “Eternal tents” and the “dwelling-places of the holy” are a possible echo. Scholars list it, but it is not certain.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 15:6-7
refs.note: Parallel: Mark 12:25. Jesus says people in the resurrection are like angels who do not marry. 1 Enoch says heavenly beings have no wives.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 53:6
refs.note: Parallel: Acts 7:52. Calling Jesus “the Righteous One” matches how 1 Enoch names the coming Righteous and Elect One.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 40:5
refs.note: Parallel: Luke 23:35. “The Chosen One” as a title for the Messiah also appears in 1 Enoch.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 45:3
refs.note: Parallel: Luke 23:35. “The Chosen One” as a title for the Messiah also appears in 1 Enoch.

refs.label: 1 Enoch 47:1-4
refs.note: Parallel: Revelation 6:9-10. The cry of the killed righteous for justice is close to the prayer of the righteous in 1 Enoch 47.

refs.label: Jude 1:9
refs.note: This book is not in our Bible. The Assumption of Moses survives only in part, and the section Jude seems to use is missing.

refs.label: The Book of Jubilees 3:27-29
refs.note: Parallel: Galatians 3:19. Paul says the law was given through angels. In Jubilees the angel of the presence writes for Moses.

refs.label: Damascus Document 7:17
refs.note: Named: 2 Timothy 3:8. Paul names Jannes and Jambres, who opposed Moses. The Old Testament never names them. Our Jasher names them. Our Damascus Document has “Jochanneh and his brother”, which scholars connect to Jannes and Jambres. There was also an old Book of Jannes and Jambres, which is mostly lost and is not in our Bible.

refs.label: The Book of Jasher 79:27
refs.note: Named: 2 Timothy 3:8. Paul names Jannes and Jambres, who opposed Moses. The Old Testament never names them. Our Jasher names them. Our Damascus Document has “Jochanneh and his brother”, which scholars connect to Jannes and Jambres. There was also an old Book of Jannes and Jambres, which is mostly lost and is not in our Bible.

refs.label: Ascension of Isaiah 5:11-14
refs.note: Allusion: Hebrews 11:37. “Sawn apart” is not recorded in the Old Testament. An old Jewish tradition says Isaiah was sawn in two, and the Ascension of Isaiah tells it.

refs.label: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 7:5
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 22:37-40. Loving God and loving your neighbor are paired in the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs (Dan and Issachar). Jesus draws his two commands from Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18.

refs.label: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 5:5
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 22:37-40. Loving God and loving your neighbor are paired in the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs (Dan and Issachar). Jesus draws his two commands from Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18.

refs.label: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 3:6
refs.note: Parallel: 1 Thessalonians 2:16. “Wrath has come upon them to the uttermost” is the same wording as in the Testament of Levi. Some scholars think one borrowed from the other.

refs.label: 2 Maccabees 7:7-9
refs.note: Allusion: Hebrews 11:35. “Tortured, not accepting deliverance, to obtain a better resurrection” points to the seven brothers and their mother in 2 Maccabees 7, who refused release and trusted in the resurrection.

refs.label: 2 Maccabees 7:14
refs.note: Allusion: Hebrews 11:35. “Tortured, not accepting deliverance, to obtain a better resurrection” points to the seven brothers and their mother in 2 Maccabees 7, who refused release and trusted in the resurrection.

refs.label: 1 Maccabees 4:52-59
refs.note: Named: John 10:22. The Feast of Dedication (Hanukkah) is not in the Old Testament. 1 Maccabees tells how Judas Maccabeus cleansed the temple and began the feast.

refs.label: 2 Maccabees 10:5-8
refs.note: Named: John 10:22. The Feast of Dedication (Hanukkah) is not in the Old Testament. 1 Maccabees tells how Judas Maccabeus cleansed the temple and began the feast.

refs.label: 1 Maccabees 1:54
refs.note: Allusion: Matthew 24:15. “The abomination of desolation” is from Daniel. 1 Maccabees records the time it was set up on the altar, which is the event Jesus' words recall.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13
refs.note: Allusion: Matthew 27:43. The leaders mock Jesus: “He trusts in God, let God deliver him.” In Wisdom 2 the wicked say nearly the same about the righteous man who calls himself God's son.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16-20
refs.note: Allusion: Matthew 27:43. The leaders mock Jesus: “He trusts in God, let God deliver him.” In Wisdom 2 the wicked say nearly the same about the righteous man who calls himself God's son.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25-26
refs.note: Parallel: Hebrews 1:3. Hebrews calls the Son the radiance of God's glory. Wisdom calls wisdom a pure emanation of God's glory and a reflection of everlasting light. The rare Greek word for “radiance” is in both.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 13:1-5
refs.note: Parallel: Romans 1:19-25. Paul's argument that people can know God from creation, and that idol worship leads to wickedness, closely follows Wisdom 13-14.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 14:22-27
refs.note: Parallel: Romans 1:19-25. Paul's argument that people can know God from creation, and that idol worship leads to wickedness, closely follows Wisdom 13-14.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 2:23-24
refs.note: Parallel: Romans 5:12. Death entering the world is also described in Wisdom 2. Wisdom says it came by the devil's envy. Paul says it came through sin.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 6:3
refs.note: Parallel: Romans 13:1. Rulers have power given by God, in both Paul and Wisdom 6.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8
refs.note: Parallel: 1 Corinthians 6:2. “The saints will judge the world” is close to “They will judge nations” in Wisdom 3.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 9:15
refs.note: Parallel: 2 Corinthians 5:1-4. The body as an earthly tent that weighs us down appears in both.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:5-6
refs.note: Parallel: 1 Peter 1:6-7. Faith tested like gold in the fire is also pictured in Wisdom 3.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 5:17-20
refs.note: Parallel: Ephesians 6:13-17. God's armor of righteousness, a shield and a sword is also in Wisdom 5. Both draw on Isaiah 59:17.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:15-16
refs.note: Parallel: Hebrews 4:12. God's word as a sharp sword is in both. Isaiah 49:2 is a likely source for the image.

refs.label: Wisdom of Solomon 15:7
refs.note: Parallel: Romans 9:21. The potter making different vessels from the same clay is in both. Isaiah and Jeremiah use the picture too.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 28:2
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 6:12-15. Forgive your neighbor and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray. Jesus teaches the same.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 7:14
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 6:7. Do not babble or repeat your words in prayer.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 51:23-27
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 11:28-30. “Take my yoke upon you and find rest” is close to “Put your neck under the yoke” and “I found much rest” in Sirach 51.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 11:18-19
refs.note: Parallel: Luke 12:19-20. The rich fool who says “I have found rest, now I will eat my goods” is very close to Sirach's rich man.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 29:10-11
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 6:19-20. Storing up treasure by giving is also taught in Sirach 29 and Tobit 4.

refs.label: Tobit 4:9
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 6:19-20. Storing up treasure by giving is also taught in Sirach 29 and Tobit 4.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 9:8
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 5:28. Do not gaze on another's beauty. Jesus goes further and speaks of the look of lust.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 7:32-35
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 25:36. Visiting the sick and giving bread to the hungry and clothes to the naked are also taught in Sirach and Tobit.

refs.label: Tobit 4:16
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 25:36. Visiting the sick and giving bread to the hungry and clothes to the naked are also taught in Sirach and Tobit.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 37:2
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 26:38. “Sorrow even to death” has similar wording to “grief even to death” in Sirach. This is a possible echo.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 5:11
refs.note: Parallel: James 1:19. “Swift to hear” appears in both.

refs.label: Wisdom of Sirach 15:11-13
refs.note: Parallel: James 1:13. Do not say God makes you do wrong. James and Sirach teach this.

refs.label: Tobit 4:15
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 7:12 + Luke 6:31. The Golden Rule in its “do not do” form: “What you hate, do to no one.” Jesus gives it in positive form.

refs.label: Tobit 4:7-8
refs.note: Parallel: Luke 14:13-14. Giving to the poor is taught in both.

refs.label: Tobit 12:15
refs.note: Parallel: Revelation 8:2. The seven angels who stand before God appear in both. Only Tobit names them as seven holy angels.

refs.label: Tobit 13:16-17
refs.note: Parallel: Revelation 21:18-21. The new Jerusalem built with precious stones and gold appears in both.

refs.label: Susanna 1:46
refs.note: Parallel: Matthew 27:24. Declaring yourself clean of innocent blood is in both. Pilate says it of Jesus. Daniel says it about Susanna.

refs.label: Prayer of Manasseh 1:1-3
refs.note: Named: 2 Chronicles 33:18-19. The Bible says Manasseh's prayer was written down. The Prayer of Manasseh in our Bible is an old prayer with that title. Scholars doubt it is the original prayer, which is lost.
